source: RFC 4493 section 4 and the NIST SP 800-38B example set
note: CMAC as SDLS uses it for frame authentication. CCSDS 355.0-B-2 clause E2a requires a 256-bit key, which is why the AES-256 cases matter here and the AES-128 ones are carried as the more widely published cross-check. All values are transcribed from the published example sets; they are not recomputed here, because the published sets are the authority. Test keys only, never real keys.

encode.name: aes128-empty-message
encode.note: Example 1 of RFC 4493 section 4: key 2b7e151628aed2a6abf7158809cf4f3c, empty message, MAC bb1d6929e95937287fa37d129b756746. This is the case that exercises the subkey path with no full block.

encode.name: aes128-one-block
encode.note: Example 2 of RFC 4493 section 4: the first 16 octets of the standard message, exactly one block, no padding.

encode.name: aes128-partial-final-block
encode.note: Example 3 of RFC 4493 section 4: 40 octets, so two full blocks and a partial third that takes the padding-and-K2 path.

encode.name: aes128-four-blocks
encode.note: Example 4 of RFC 4493 section 4: 64 octets, four full blocks, so the final block takes the K1 path with no padding.

encode.name: aes256-empty-message
encode.note: Mlen 0. The case CCSDS 355.0-B-2 clause E2a cares about most, since SDLS mandates a 256-bit key. Empty message takes the padding-and-K2 path. Transcribed from the published NIST example set.

encode.name: aes256-one-block
encode.note: Mlen 16: exactly one block, K1 path, no padding. Transcribed from the published NIST example set.

encode.name: aes256-partial-final-block
encode.note: Mlen 20: one full block and a 4-octet remainder, so the final block is padded and uses K2. Transcribed from the published NIST example set.

encode.name: aes256-four-blocks
encode.note: Mlen 64: four full blocks, K1 path. Transcribed from the published NIST example set.
